adjudicated.jp: 「んなわけないでしょ！！　サンドイッチでしょ！」
adjudicated.en: Touko: "'s not that at all you know!!! It's a sandwich you know!"
adjudicated.assessment: The clipped Japanese opening is colloquial but grammatical in context. The English begins with a stranded contraction and adds a repeated tag, producing malformed dialogue rather than equivalent conversational compression.
adjudicated.remedy: Use a grammatical emphatic denial before identifying it as a sandwich.

adjudicated.jp: 「自分しか、自分の心配をしてくれる人間がいないのは、つらいだろ？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Having no human alive, none outside of you, that worry about you... it's painful, right?"
comments: Hyperliteral as this is either her refusal to see mankind or, well, meant hyperliterally. See CCC0000: this is The Sentence. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source says it is painful when nobody but oneself will worry about oneself. The English adds the absolute claim that no human is alive, then damages the relation with a subject-verb agreement error.
adjudicated.remedy: Express that being the only person who worries about oneself is painful.

highlights.text: Having no human alive, none outside of you, that worry about you

adjudicated.jp: 「何言ってるのかわからない」

adjudicated.remedy: Use a grammatical equivalent such as 'I don't know what you're talking about.'

adjudicated.jp: 「……あんまいい死に方できないぞ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...that ain't a really good way to die ya know."
comments: It's like he knows that she's starving herself, despite never figuring it out in most routes until he sees her pass out in front of him. Suspecting it's another thing he knows - it's certainly not the first summer he's known her - and its origin is simply going to become detached as the Game starts.

There's also some stuff about 'anma'/'anman' that strike me as a pun, given how 'anma' also means blind person (who traditionally gave the 'anma' massages), especially given that Touko goes blind. But that may be overthinking things.
Finally, see CCD0020B, where this line refers to himself. May be just an older revision, though. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source warns that she will not come to a good end or die well. The English recasts the conduct itself as a method of dying and adds marked dialect.
adjudicated.remedy: Render the warning as not coming to a good end.

highlights.text: that ain't a really good way to die ya know
